definition_zh: 宽慰；缓解；救济；浮雕；换班
definition_en: the good feeling that comes when pain, worry, or trouble stops or becomes less
core_image: 压在肩上的重物被突然搬走，人长长吐出一口气
scene: 手术室的灯灭后，医生摘下口罩说手术很成功，走廊里的人同时松下了肩膀。When the doctor said the operation had succeeded, a wave of relief spread through the corridor.
sceneCN: 这里 relief 是「宽慰、如释重负」（第 1 个义项：痛苦或忧虑解除后的轻松）；句意：医生说手术成功后，走廊里的人们感到一阵宽慰。

pos.zh: 宽慰；缓解；救济；浮雕；换班

derivatives.zh: 由名词 relief 回溯拉丁动词，义为「减轻；缓解」
relieve 加 -ed 构成，义为「感到宽慰的」
relieve 加否定前缀 un- 与 -ed，义为「未获缓解的；单调的」

senses.title: The end of pain or worry
senses.definition: the pleasant feeling you have when pain, anxiety, or a difficult situation ends
senses.definitionCN: 疼痛、焦虑或困境结束后所产生的轻松愉快感
senses.example: She felt a huge sense of relief when the exam results finally arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 考试成绩终于公布时，她感到如释重负。
senses.why: The Latin verb relevare means to raise or lift up, so the core image is a weight being lifted off the body.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词 relevare 表示「抬起、举起」，所以核心画面是压在身上的重物被抬走，紧绷随之松开。

senses.title: Help for people in trouble
senses.definition: money, food, or other help given to people who are in need, especially after a disaster
senses.definitionCN: 给予困境中的人们的钱、食物或其他帮助，尤指灾后援助
senses.example: Relief supplies reached the village two days after the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水过后两天，救援物资运抵了村庄。
senses.why: If the core image is lifting a weight, then lifting people out of hardship naturally gives the word the sense of aid itself.
senses.whyCN: 既然核心画面是把重物抬起，那么把人从苦难中托起来，就自然延伸出「援助」这一义项。

senses.title: A design raised above a surface
senses.definition: a design cut into stone or metal so that it stands out above the flat background
senses.definitionCN: 在石头或金属上雕刻出的、凸出于平面的图案
senses.example: The coin shows the queen's head in relief.
senses.exampleCN: 这枚硬币上铸有女王头像的浮雕。
senses.why: The raised part of a carving is literally lifted above the surface, which matches the lifting image at the heart of the word.
senses.whyCN: 浮雕凸起的部分正是从平面被「抬起来」的，与这个词核心的抬起画面完全吻合。

senses.title: A shift that takes over a duty
senses.definition: a person or group that takes over a job from someone else so that the work can continue
senses.definitionCN: 从他人手中接过工作、使工作中断得以继续的人或班组
senses.example: The night relief arrived at six in the morning.
senses.exampleCN: 夜班接替人员早上六点到了。
senses.why: Passing a load from one pair of shoulders to another is the same lifting picture, applied to work shifts.
senses.whyCN: 把重担从一副肩膀交到另一副肩膀，仍是「抬起并转移」这个画面，用在轮班场景里就成了换班。

intro.en: Relief comes through Old French from the Latin verb relevare, built from the prefix re- and the verb levare.
intro.cn: relief 经由古法语来自拉丁动词 relevare，该词由前缀 re- 与动词 levare 组合而成。

items.en: Relevare means to raise up, lift, or lighten, and is formed from re- plus levare.
items.cn: relevare 意为抬起、举起或减轻，由 re- 与 levare 构成。

items.en: Levare comes from the adjective levis, light in weight, the same root found in levity.
items.cn: levare 源自形容词 levis「重量轻的」，这个词根也见于 levity。

items.en: Relevium names a payment raised from a tenant, showing the idea of something lifted up.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 relevium 指向佃户征收的一笔款项，同样带有「被抬起之物」的意味。

items.en: Old French relief carries the senses of a raising, of help, and of a remainder.
items.cn: 古法语 relief 同时有「抬起」「帮助」「剩余部分」几层意思。

items.en: English borrows the word for help given to someone in trouble and for a raised carving.
items.cn: 英语借入这个词，用于表示给予困境中人的帮助，也指凸起的雕刻。

items.en: Modern English keeps the eased feeling, the aid, the raised carving, and the relieving shift.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了宽慰感、援助、浮雕以及换班这几层含义。

note.en: Relief belongs to a re- and lev- family about lifting weight, and it sits near words for making trouble smaller.
note.cn: relief 属于由 re- 与 lev- 构成、表示「抬起重量」的词族，同时又与表示「使麻烦变小」的词相邻。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on Latin levare, to lift, so the memory hooks mostly involve lifting a weight.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语 levare「举起」之上，所以记忆钩子大多围绕「把重物抬走」。

normal.en: Re- plus lev- gives the picture of lifting something up again, and the weight comes off.
normal.cn: 前缀 re- 加词根 lev-，画面是把东西重新抬起来，重量随之离开。

normal.en: Compare elevator: both words lift, one lifts people, the other lifts weight off a mind.
normal.cn: 对比 elevator：两者都在「抬起」，一个载人，一个把重量从心头抬走。

normal.en: The pair relief and relieve differs only by the last letter, noun against verb.
normal.cn: relief 与 relieve 只差最后一个字母，一个是名词，一个是动词。

normal.en: A sigh of relief is literally the sound of a lifted weight.
normal.cn: a sigh of relief 字面上就是重物被抬走时那口长气。

normal.en: Disaster relief is help that lifts a whole town back onto its feet.
normal.cn: disaster relief 是把整座城镇重新托起来的援助。

abstract.en: Imagine a backpack of stones sliding off your back; your shoulders drop and you breathe out.
abstract.cn: 想象一包石头从背上滑落，肩膀塌下来，你长长呼气。

abstract.en: Think of a carved coin: the head is pushed up out of the flat metal.
abstract.cn: 想一枚硬币，头像被从平整的金属里顶出来。

abstract.en: Picture a relay of workers: one steps away, the next takes the load.
abstract.cn: 想象工人接力：一个人退下，下一个人接过重物。

examples.en: She breathed a sigh of relief when she heard the news.
examples.cn: 听到这个消息，她松了一口气。

examples.en: The government sent relief to the flooded region.
examples.cn: 政府向洪涝地区运送了救援物资。

examples.en: The statue is carved in relief on the temple wall.
examples.cn: 庙墙上雕着这座雕像的浮雕。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞丽福」——想象瑞丽小城送来福气，紧绷的心一下松开；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（再次、向后）+ levare（举起，源自 levis「轻」）构成 relevare（抬起、减轻），经古法语 relief 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: One image of a lifted weight grows into four senses: the eased mind, the aid given, the raised carving, and the shift that takes over.
sensesIntro.cn: 「抬起重量」这一个画面长出四个义项：心里的轻松、给出的援助、凸起的浮雕，以及接过工作的换班。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heavy weight lifted from the shoulders.
core.cn: 核心意象：压在肩上的重物被抬起搬走。

branches.en: The mind feels the weight go, so relief names the eased feeling.
branches.cn: 心里感到重量消失，于是 relief 指那种松弛下来的感觉。

branches.en: Lifting a person out of hardship becomes the name for the help itself.
branches.cn: 把人从困境中托起来，进一步成为「援助」的名称。

branches.en: A carving stands up above the flat surface, exactly like something lifted.
branches.cn: 浮雕高出平面，正像被抬起的东西。

branches.en: A load passed to fresh hands becomes the relieving shift.
branches.cn: 重担交到新的人手上，就成了接替的班次。

branches.en: Both the eased feeling and the aid come from the same upward movement.
branches.cn: 心中的松弛与外来的援助都源自同一个向上的动作。

intro.en: Relief is built from a Latin prefix and a Latin root, with a French noun ending carried into English.
intro.cn: relief 由拉丁前缀、拉丁词根以及传入英语的法语名词词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin prefix re- means back or again, and levare means to lift, so together they describe lifting a burden away.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁前缀 re- 表示「向后、再次」，levare 表示「举起」，合起来就是「把重担抬走」。

items.example: The prefix re- returns in relieve and remove.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 也出现在 relieve 与 remove 中。

items.example: The root lev- also appears in elevate and levity.
items.exampleCN: 词根 lev- 也出现在 elevate 与 levity 中。

items.example: Levare is the verb behind relief and relieve.
items.exampleCN: levare 是 relief 与 relieve 背后的动词。

items.example: Levis is the source of the lev- root in this family.
items.exampleCN: levis 是这一词族中 lev- 词根的来源。

items.meaningCN: 表示结果或状态的名词词尾
items.example: The ending -ief carries the French form into English relief.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ief 把法语形式带进了英语 relief。

items.meaning: to lift up again, to ease
items.example: Relevare joins re- and levare into a single verb.
items.exampleCN: relevare 把 re- 与 levare 合成了一个动词。

items.example: Levity uses the same levis root for lightness of behaviour.
items.exampleCN: levity 用同一个 levis 词根表示举止上的轻。

items.example: Alleviate adds ad- to the same levis root.
items.exampleCN: alleviate 在同一个 levis 词根前加了 ad-。

definition_zh: 缓解；减轻；接替；使摆脱；调剂
definition_en: to make pain, worry, or a difficult situation less serious
core_image: 拧得过紧的阀门被慢慢松开，压力随之下降
scene: 护士调慢了输液速度，药物在几分钟内让病人的疼痛明显减轻。The nurse slowed the drip, and the drug began to relieve his pain within minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 relieve 是「缓解」（第 1 个义项：使疼痛或问题变轻）；句意：护士调慢了输液速度，药物在几分钟内开始缓解他的疼痛。

pos.zh: 缓解；减轻；接替；使摆脱；调剂

senses.title: To make pain or trouble less severe
senses.definition: to make a feeling of pain, worry, or pressure weaker or easier to bear
senses.definitionCN: 使疼痛、忧虑或压力的感觉变弱、变得容易承受
senses.example: This medicine will relieve your headache in about half an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药大约半小时后能缓解你的头痛。
senses.why: The Latin source means to lift a weight, so easing pain is pictured as taking part of the load off.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词源意为「抬起重量」，因此缓解疼痛被想象成把部分负担从身上拿走。

senses.title: To take over a duty from someone
senses.definition: to take the place of someone who is on duty so that they can rest
senses.definitionCN: 替换正在值班的人，使其可以休息
senses.example: A fresh guard came to relieve the man at the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 一名新哨兵来替换门口的那个人。
senses.why: If a load can be lifted and handed on, then a duty can be lifted from one person and given to another.
senses.whyCN: 既然重物可以抬起并转交，那么职责也能从一个人身上卸下、交给另一个人。

senses.title: To free someone from something unpleasant
senses.definition: to take away a duty, worry, or possession from someone, often formally
senses.definitionCN: 把某项职责、忧虑或财物从某人身上拿走，常用于正式语境
senses.example: Let me relieve you of that heavy bag.
senses.exampleCN: 让我帮你拿那个重包吧。
senses.why: Lifting a weight off a person is the same motion as taking a burden or duty away from them.
senses.whyCN: 把人身上的重量抬走，与替他拿走负担或职务是同一个动作。

senses.title: To add variety to something dull
senses.definition: to make a boring or uniform situation more interesting by adding something different
senses.definitionCN: 通过加入变化，使枯燥或单调的场面变得有趣
senses.example: A few jokes relieved the tension in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 几个笑话缓解了房间里的紧张气氛。
senses.why: Relief is a lifting of pressure, and a dull stretch of time is felt as pressure that a change lifts away.
senses.whyCN: relief 的本质是卸下压力，而漫长的沉闷也像一种压力，变化正是把它抬走。

intro.en: Relieve comes from Old French relever, which descends from the Latin verb relevare.
intro.cn: relieve 来自古法语 relever，后者可追溯到拉丁动词 relevare。

items.en: Relevare combines re- with levare, to lift, and means to raise up or lighten.
items.cn: relevare 由 re- 与 levare「举起」组合，意为抬起或减轻。

items.en: Levare is built on levis, light in weight, which also gives levity.
items.cn: levare 建立在 levis「重量轻」之上，这个词根也产生了 levity。

items.en: Colloquial forms of relevare spread through the spoken language of the late empire.
items.cn: relevare 的口语形式在帝国晚期的日常语言中传播开来。

items.en: Old French relever means to raise again, to help up, and to ease.
items.cn: 古法语 relever 表示重新举起、扶起以及缓解。

items.en: English adopts relieve for easing pain, taking over a duty, and freeing someone of a burden.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪引入 relieve，用于缓解疼痛、接替职责以及替人卸下负担。

items.en: The modern verb keeps all three threads and adds the lighter sense of adding variety.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了这三条线索，并增添了「调剂、增加变化」这层较轻的含义。

note.en: Relieve is the verb behind relief and shares its lifting root with several light-related words.
note.cn: relieve 是名词 relief 背后的动词，并与若干表示「轻」的词共享抬起的词根。

normalIntro.en: Relieve is the verb form of the re- and lev- family, so its hooks all circle the idea of lifting.
normalIntro.cn: relieve 是 re- 与 lev- 词族的动词形式，所以记忆钩子都围绕「抬起」。

normal.en: Say the pair together: relief is the state, relieve is the act of bringing it about.
normal.cn: 把这一对一起记：relief 是状态，relieve 是带来这种状态的动作。

normal.en: The root lev- also lifts in elevate and lever, both about raising something.
normal.cn: 词根 lev- 在 elevate 和 lever 里同样表示「抬起」。

normal.en: Relieve someone of a bag means taking the weight into your own hand.
normal.cn: relieve someone of a bag 就是把重量接到自己手里。

normal.en: The past participle relieved doubles as the everyday adjective for feeling better.
normal.cn: 过去分词 relieved 同时也常用作形容词，表示「放心了」。

normal.en: Remember the fixed phrase relieve the pressure when talking about stress at work.
normal.cn: 谈到工作压力时，记住固定搭配 relieve the pressure。

abstract.en: Picture a valve turning loose and steam hissing out of a blocked pipe.
abstract.cn: 想象一个阀门被拧松，蒸汽从堵塞的管道里嘶嘶冒出。

abstract.en: Imagine handing a heavy suitcase to a friend at the top of the stairs.
abstract.cn: 想象在楼梯顶端把沉重的行李箱交给朋友。

abstract.en: See two guards saluting as one walks away and the other steps into place.
abstract.cn: 想象两名卫兵敬礼，一个走开，另一个站到岗位上。

examples.en: These tablets should relieve the swelling within a day.
examples.cn: 这些药片应该在一天之内缓解肿胀。

examples.en: I was relieved to hear that everyone was safe.
examples.cn: 听说大家都平安，我松了一口气。

examples.en: A new team will relieve the workers at midnight.
examples.cn: 一支新的队伍将在午夜替换这些工人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞丽舞」——想象瑞丽的舞蹈让紧绷的人放松下来；只是谐音联想，并非词源。

root: 古法语 relever，源自拉丁语 relevare（re-「再次」+ levare「举起」，levis「轻」），核心为「把重量抬起」。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses are versions of the same act of lifting: lifting pain, lifting a duty, lifting a burden, lifting dullness.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项都是同一个「抬起」动作的不同版本：抬起疼痛、抬起职责、抬起负担、抬起沉闷。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tight valve loosened so that pressure falls.
core.cn: 核心意象：拧紧的阀门被松开，压力随之下降。

branches.en: Loosening pressure is felt first as less pain.
branches.cn: 松开压力最先被感受为疼痛变轻。

branches.en: Lifting a duty off one person puts it on another, which is the relieving shift.
branches.cn: 把职责从一人身上卸下交给另一人，就是接替。

branches.en: Taking a heavy thing out of someone's hands is the sense of freeing.
branches.cn: 把重物从某人手里拿走，就是使其摆脱。

branches.en: A dull stretch is pressure too, so a change relieves it.
branches.cn: 沉闷的时段也是一种压力，变化正是在缓解它。

branches.en: All three come from the same movement of weight leaving a person.
branches.cn: 前三项都来自重量离开同一个人的同一个动作。

intro.en: Relieve keeps the Latin prefix, the Latin root, and a French verb ending in one short word.
intro.cn: relieve 在短短一个词里保留了拉丁前缀、拉丁词根和法语动词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin re- adds the idea of back or again, and levare supplies the lifting, so the verb means to lift back up.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁前缀 re- 带来「回、再」的意思，levare 提供「举起」，合起来就是「重新抬起」。

items.example: Re- appears again in remove and renew.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 也出现在 remove 与 renew 中。

items.example: The lev- root also lifts in lever.
items.exampleCN: lev- 词根在 lever 中也表示抬起。

items.example: Levare supplies the second half of relieve.
items.exampleCN: levare 提供 relieve 的后半部分。

items.meaningCN: 标记动词不定式形式的词尾
items.example: The final -e comes from the French infinitive relever.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -e 来自法语不定式 relever。

items.example: Relevare is the direct ancestor of relever.
items.exampleCN: relevare 是 relever 的直接来源。

items.meaning: the easing of pain or worry

items.exampleCN: relief 去掉动词词尾，保留同一词根。

items.meaning: a bar used to lift or move something
items.example: Lever is the lev- root in its plainest lifting form.
items.exampleCN: lever 是 lev- 词根最直白的「抬起」形式。

items.meaning: to raise to a higher position
items.example: Elevate adds e- to the same lev- root.
items.exampleCN: elevate 在同一个 lev- 词根前加了 e-。

derivatives.zh: religion 加 -ous 构成，义为「宗教的；虔诚的」
religious 加 -ly 构成，义为「虔诚地；一丝不苟地」

senses.title: Belief in a divine power
senses.definition: the belief that a god or gods exist and that people should worship them
senses.definitionCN: 相信存在神并应当对其崇拜的信念
senses.example: Religion gave the villagers comfort after the earthquake.
senses.exampleCN: 地震之后，宗教信仰给了村民们安慰。
senses.why: If the old root means to bind, then religion is the cord that ties a person to the divine.
senses.whyCN: 如果古老的词根意为「系紧」，那么宗教就是把人与神明系在一起的那根绳索。

senses.title: A system of faith and worship
senses.definition: one of the organized systems of faith, ritual, and moral teaching followed by a group
senses.definitionCN: 一群人遵循的、由信仰、仪式与道德教义组成的有组织体系
senses.example: Buddhism is one of the great religions of Asia.
senses.exampleCN: 佛教是亚洲的伟大宗教之一。
senses.why: A single binding cord becomes a shared framework when a whole community is tied by the same beliefs and rites.
senses.whyCN: 当整个群体被同一套信仰与仪式系在一起，那一根绳索就变成了一套共同体系。

senses.title: Something pursued with devotion
senses.definition: an activity that someone treats with the seriousness and devotion normally given to a faith
senses.definitionCN: 某人以近乎信仰的认真与投入对待的活动
senses.example: For him, fitness is a religion rather than a hobby.
senses.exampleCN: 对他而言，健身不是爱好，而是一种信仰。
senses.why: The binding force of faith can be transferred to any practice that rules a person's days, hence the figurative use.
senses.whyCN: 信仰那种系住人的力量可以转移到任何支配日常生活的活动上，于是有了这个比喻用法。

intro.en: The origin of religion is debated. Most reference works point to Latin religare, to bind fast, while others argue for relegere, to read over again.
intro.cn: religion 的词源存在争议：多数辞书认为来自拉丁语 religare「系紧」，也有学者主张来自 relegere「反复阅读、重新重视」。

items.en: Religare combines re- with ligare, to bind, and means to tie fast.
items.cn: religare 由 re- 与 ligare「捆绑」组合，意为牢牢系住。

items.en: Relegere means to read over again or to go over carefully, and is the rival explanation.
items.cn: relegere 意为反复阅读或仔细重温，是另一种解释的来源。

items.en: Religio in classical Latin covers scruple, reverence, and the fear of the gods.
items.cn: 古典拉丁语 religio 涵盖顾忌、敬畏以及对神明的畏惧。

items.en: Old French religion names a monastic order as well as a system of faith.
items.cn: 古法语 religion 既指修会，也指信仰体系。

items.en: English adopts religion for a system of faith and for the state of being devout.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪引入 religion，指信仰体系与虔诚的状态。

items.en: The modern word keeps the system sense and adds the playful sense of a devoted pursuit.
items.cn: 现代英语保留「体系」之义，并增添了「执着追求」这一戏谑用法。

note.en: Religion sits beside words for belief, and it looks like several Latin words built on the same re- prefix.
note.cn: religion 与表示「信念」的词相邻，外形上也与若干由 re- 开头的拉丁词相近。

entries.definition: relating to religion or believing strongly in it
entries.definitionCN: 宗教的；虔诚的，由 religion 加 -ous 构成

entries.definition: in a very regular and careful way
entries.definitionCN: 一丝不苟地；虔诚地

entries.definition: to bind together, a rare technical verb
entries.definitionCN: 捆扎；系紧，是罕见的技术用词，与 religion 共享 ligare 词根

entries.definition: strong belief in a religion or in someone
entries.definitionCN: 信仰；信任，侧重内心的确信

entries.definition: a feeling that something is true or real
entries.definitionCN: 信念；看法，范围比 religion 更宽

entries.definition: a formal statement of religious belief
entries.definitionCN: 信条；教义，是宗教信念的正式表述

normalIntro.en: The word is usually explained through Latin ligare, to bind, so most hooks use the image of a tie.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词通常用拉丁语 ligare「捆绑」来解释，所以记忆钩子多用「系住」的画面。

normal.en: Religion and ligament share the lig- root of binding; one ties a person to a faith.
normal.cn: religion 与 ligament 共享表示「捆绑」的 lig- 词根，一个系住人，一个系住骨。

normal.en: The adjective religious adds -ous, and the adverb religiously adds -ly after that.
normal.cn: 形容词 religious 加了 -ous，副词 religiously 再在其后加 -ly。

normal.en: Religiously also means doing something very regularly, as if it were a ritual.
normal.cn: religiously 还表示极为规律地做某事，像是在行仪式。

normal.en: Freedom of religion is a fixed phrase worth learning as one block.
normal.cn: freedom of religion 是值得整块记住的固定表达。

normal.en: Remember that the binding explanation is the usual one but not the only hypothesis.
normal.cn: 记住「捆绑」是通行解释，但并非唯一假说。

abstract.en: Picture a rope looped around a person and tied to a high stone.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绳子绕过一个人，系在高处的石头上。

abstract.en: See a whole village kneeling in the same direction at dawn.
abstract.cn: 想象黎明时整个村庄朝同一个方向跪拜。

abstract.en: Think of a runner who treats a morning run like a sacred duty.
abstract.cn: 想一位把晨跑当成神圣义务的跑者。

examples.en: Religion has shaped the art and music of this region.
examples.cn: 宗教塑造了这个地区的艺术与音乐。

examples.en: The law protects freedom of religion for every citizen.
examples.cn: 法律保护每位公民的宗教信仰自由。

examples.en: He follows his religion with great care.
examples.cn: 他非常认真地奉行自己的宗教。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞丽珍」——想象把珍视的信念系在身上；只是谐音联想，与真实词源无关。

root: 一般认为来自拉丁语 religare（re-「牢牢地」+ ligare「捆绑」），另有 relegere（反复阅读）一说，词源存争议。

sensesIntro.en: From one binding cord come the personal belief, the organized system, and the devotion given to anything at all.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一根系紧的绳索，长出个人的信仰、有组织的体系，以及对任何事物的执着投入。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rope tying a person back to something sacred.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条把人与神圣之物系在一起的绳索。

branches.en: The tie is felt first as personal belief.
branches.cn: 这根绳索最先被感受为个人的信仰。

branches.en: When a community shares the tie, it becomes an organized system.
branches.cn: 当整个群体共享这根绳索，它就成为有组织的体系。

branches.en: The same binding force can grip a hobby, giving the figurative sense.
branches.cn: 同样的系缚之力也能抓住一项爱好，产生比喻义。

branches.en: Personal belief and shared system are two scales of the same bond.
branches.cn: 个人信仰与共同体系是同一种纽带的两个尺度。

branches.en: Both a church and a cherished routine rule the order of a day.
branches.cn: 教会与珍视的日常习惯都支配着一天的秩序。

intro.en: Religion is a Latin noun with a prefix, a root, and a suffix, all carried into English through French.
intro.cn: religion 是一个拉丁名词，含前缀、词根与词尾，经法语进入英语。

latinIntro.en: Latin re- strengthens the action, ligare means to bind, and -io names the resulting state.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁前缀 re- 加强动作，ligare 表示「捆绑」，词尾 -io 表示由此形成的状态。

items.example: Re- tightens the action in religare.
items.exampleCN: 在 religare 中，前缀 re- 加强了动作。

items.example: The lig- root also binds in ligament.
items.exampleCN: lig- 词根在 ligament 中也表示系缚。

items.example: Ligare is the verb behind the lig- root.
items.exampleCN: ligare 是 lig- 词根背后的动词。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或结果的名词词尾
items.example: The ending -io turns the verb into a noun of state.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -io 把动词变成表示状态的名词。

items.example: Religare is the usual source given for religion.
items.exampleCN: religare 是 religion 通常被追溯到的来源。

items.example: Religio already carries both fear and worship.
items.exampleCN: religio 同时带有畏惧与崇拜两层意思。

items.meaning: a band of tissue that ties bones together
items.example: Ligament keeps the binding sense of ligare.
items.exampleCN: ligament 保留了 ligare 的「系缚」含义。

items.meaning: a duty that ties a person to an action
items.example: Obligation adds ob- to the same ligare root.
items.exampleCN: obligation 在同一个 ligare 词根前加了 ob-。

senses.title: Connected with religion
senses.definition: relating to religion, its beliefs, or its practices
senses.definitionCN: 与宗教、其信仰或仪式有关的
senses.example: The building is used for religious ceremonies.
senses.exampleCN: 这座建筑用于宗教仪式。
senses.why: The adjective is simply the noun religion with a Latin ending added, so it describes anything that belongs to that binding system.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是名词 religion 加上拉丁词尾，因此描述一切属于那套系缚体系的东西。

senses.title: Believing strongly in a faith
senses.definition: believing firmly in a religion and taking part in its practices regularly
senses.definitionCN: 坚定地信仰某种宗教并规律参与其仪式
senses.example: Her grandmother was a deeply religious woman.
senses.exampleCN: 她的祖母是一位非常虔诚的女性。
senses.why: A person held tightly by the bond of faith is described with the same adjective, which shifts from belonging to devotion.
senses.whyCN: 被信仰之绳牢牢系住的人也用同一个形容词描述，词义从「属于」转向「虔诚」。

senses.title: Done with great care and regularity
senses.definition: done carefully and at fixed times, as if it were a duty
senses.definitionCN: 认真且按固定时间去做，仿佛是一项义务
senses.example: He checks the figures with religious care.
senses.exampleCN: 他以近乎虔诚的仔细核对数字。
senses.why: Someone who never misses a rite becomes the model for anyone who never misses a routine.
senses.whyCN: 从不缺席仪式的人，成了从不漏掉任何例行事务之人的范本。

intro.en: Religious is the Latin-derived adjective of religion, formed with the ending -ous.
intro.cn: religious 是由 religion 派生、带拉丁词尾 -ous 的形容词。

items.en: Religiosus describes someone careful about rites and full of scruple.
items.cn: religiosus 形容对仪式谨慎、心存顾忌的人。

items.en: The suffix -osus means full of, so religiosus means full of religious care.
items.cn: 词尾 -osus 表示「充满」，因此 religiosus 意为「满怀宗教式谨慎的」。

items.en: Old French religieus keeps both the belonging sense and the devout sense.
items.cn: 古法语 religieus 同时保留「属于宗教」与「虔诚」两层意思。

items.en: English religious first names members of a monastic order.
items.cn: 英语中的 religious 最初指修会成员。

items.en: The adjective widens to cover anything connected with faith and, figuratively, any careful routine.
items.cn: 这个形容词后来扩展到一切与信仰有关的事物，并比喻性地指任何谨慎的例行做法。

note.en: Religious is the everyday adjective of the religion family, and it stands near words for devotion and for belief.
note.cn: religious 是 religion 词族中日常使用的形容词，并与表示虔诚和信念的词相邻。

entries.definitionCN: 宗教；宗教信仰，是 religious 的名词来源

entries.definitionCN: 虔诚的；恭敬的，有时带做作之意

entries.definition: relating to the human spirit rather than the body
entries.definitionCN: 精神的；心灵的，不必然属于宗教

normalIntro.en: Religious is just religion plus the Latin ending -ous, so the hooks mostly revisit the noun.
normalIntro.cn: religious 就是 religion 加上拉丁词尾 -ous，所以记忆钩子大多回到那个名词。

normal.en: Drop the noun ending and add -ous: religion becomes religious.
normal.cn: 去掉名词词尾，加上 -ous，religion 就变成 religious。

normal.en: Add -ly and you get religiously, which also means doing something without fail.
normal.cn: 再加 -ly 得到 religiously，它也表示从不间断地做某事。

normal.en: Add the negative prefix ir- for irreligious, the opposite of devout.
normal.cn: 加否定前缀 ir- 得到 irreligious，与虔诚相反。

normal.en: Deeply religious is a very common pairing in both speech and writing.
normal.cn: deeply religious 是口语和书面语中都很常见的搭配。

normal.en: The family also contains religion and religiosity, all built on the same root.
normal.cn: 这个词族还包括 religion 和 religiosity，都建立在同一词根上。

abstract.en: Picture a person who lights the same lamp at the same hour every day.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人每天同一时刻点亮同一盏灯。

abstract.en: See hands folded and eyes lowered in a quiet room.
abstract.cn: 想象安静的房间里合起的手与低垂的眼。

abstract.en: Think of someone checking a list three times, as if it were a rite.
abstract.cn: 想一个人把清单核对三遍，仿佛在行仪式。

examples.en: The festival has both a religious and a social side.
examples.cn: 这个节日既有宗教的一面，也有社交的一面。

examples.en: She comes from a very religious family.
examples.cn: 她来自一个非常虔诚的家庭。

examples.en: He follows the training plan with religious discipline.
examples.cn: 他以近乎虔诚的自律执行训练计划。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞丽哲思」——想象瑞丽小城里有人整日哲思信仰；只是谐音联想，不是词源。

root: 拉丁语 religiosus（对仪式谨慎、心存敬畏），源自 religio；词尾 -osus 表示「充满」。

sensesIntro.en: The adjective starts as a label for things belonging to faith and widens to describe a devout person and then any careful routine.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个形容词起初标记属于信仰的事物，随后扩展到形容虔诚的人，再扩展到任何一丝不苟的例行做法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person who keeps the same rite at the same hour.
core.cn: 核心意象：每天同一时刻行同一仪式的人。

branches.en: Anything tied to the faith is labelled with the adjective.
branches.cn: 一切与信仰相关的事物都用这个形容词标记。

branches.en: A person held by the bond is called devout rather than merely belonging.
branches.cn: 被这根绳索系住的人，就从「属于」转为「虔诚」。

branches.en: Never missing a rite becomes the model for never missing a routine.
branches.cn: 从不缺席仪式，成为从不漏掉例行事务的范本。

branches.en: The belonging sense and the devout sense grow from the same root.
branches.cn: 「属于宗教」与「虔诚」两义出自同一词根。

branches.en: Both stress regularity in the service of something held sacred.
branches.cn: 两者都强调为某种被视为神圣之物而保持的规律性。

intro.en: Religious keeps the Latin root of religion and adds an adjective ending.
intro.cn: religious 保留 religion 的拉丁词根，并加上形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: The ending -osus means full of, so religiosus describes a person full of religious care.
latinIntro.cn: 词尾 -osus 表示「充满」，因此 religiosus 形容满怀宗教式谨慎的人。

items.example: The relig- root is shared with religion.
items.exampleCN: relig- 词根与 religion 共用。

items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ous 把名词变成形容词。

items.example: Religiously adds -ly to the adjective.
items.exampleCN: religiously 在形容词后加了 -ly。

items.example: Irreligious uses ir- before the letter r.
items.exampleCN: irreligious 在字母 r 前使用 ir-。

items.example: Religiosus is the direct Latin source.
items.exampleCN: religiosus 是直接的拉丁来源。

items.example: Religio supplies the stem of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: religio 提供这个形容词的词干。

items.example: Religiosity adds -ity to the same stem.
items.exampleCN: religiosity 在同一词干后加了 -ity。

items.meaning: connected with God and treated with great respect

items.exampleCN: sacred 在语义上是 religious 的近邻。

definition_zh: 不情愿的；勉强的；抗拒的
definition_en: not willing to do something and therefore slow to do it
core_image: 脚往前迈，身子却往后用力挣
scene: 父亲被劝了三次，才慢慢把手伸向那台新手机。My father was reluctant to try the new phone, and it took three attempts to persuade him.
sceneCN: 这里 reluctant 是「不情愿的」（第 1 个义项：不愿意并因此拖延）；句意：父亲不愿意尝试那部新手机，劝了三次才说服他。

pos.zh: 不情愿的；勉强的；抗拒的

derivatives.zh: reluctant 加 -ance 构成，义为「不情愿；勉强」
reluctant 加 -ly 构成，义为「不情愿地」

senses.title: Unwilling and slow to act
senses.definition: not wanting to do something and therefore hesitating or delaying
senses.definitionCN: 不想做某事，因而犹豫或拖延
senses.example: She was reluctant to lend her car to a stranger.
senses.exampleCN: 她不愿意把车借给陌生人。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to struggle against, so the core picture is a body pulled forward while something inside pulls back.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「挣扎反抗」，所以核心画面是身体被往前拉，内心却在往后挣。

senses.title: Shown in a forced or half-hearted way
senses.definition: done or given without real willingness, so it looks strained
senses.definitionCN: 并非真心愿意地做出或给出，因而显得勉强
senses.example: He gave a reluctant smile and turned away.
senses.exampleCN: 他勉强笑了笑，转过身去。
senses.why: When the inner struggle shows on the face, the adjective moves from the feeling to the visible expression.
senses.whyCN: 当内心的挣扎写在脸上，这个形容词就从描述感受转为描述可见的表情。

senses.title: Struggling against something
senses.definition: physically or inwardly resisting a force, now a rare and literary use
senses.definitionCN: 在身体或内心里抵抗某种力量，如今属少见且偏文学性的用法
senses.example: The reluctant horse refused to enter the water.
senses.exampleCN: 那匹抗拒的马不肯下水。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer of the word, where the struggle is literal rather than a matter of unwillingness.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最古老的一层，挣扎是字面意义上的，而不只是「不愿意」。

intro.en: Reluctant comes from the Latin present participle reluctans, from the verb reluctari.
intro.cn: reluctant 来自拉丁语现在分词 reluctans，源自动词 reluctari。

items.en: Reluctari means to struggle against or resist, built from re- and luctari, to wrestle.
items.cn: reluctari 意为奋力反抗，由 re- 与 luctari「摔跤、搏斗」构成。

items.en: Luctari is the verb behind luctatio, a wrestling match.
items.cn: luctari 是表示摔跤比赛的 luctatio 背后的动词。

items.en: The participle reluctans describes someone actively struggling back.
items.cn: 分词 reluctans 描述正在用力往回挣的人。

items.en: English borrows reluctant first in the literal sense of struggling against.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪先借入其「奋力抵抗」的字面义。

items.en: The word settles into the milder everyday sense of unwilling and hesitant.
items.cn: 这个词后来固定为更温和的日常义：不愿意、犹豫。

note.en: Reluctant belongs to a small family of unwillingness, and its Latin root is about wrestling.
note.cn: reluctant 属于表示「不愿意」的小词族，其拉丁词根与摔跤有关。

entries.definition: the feeling of not wanting to do something
entries.definitionCN: 不情愿；勉强，是 reluctant 的名词形式

entries.definition: in an unwilling way

entries.definition: to struggle against, an obsolete verb
entries.definitionCN: 反抗；挣扎，是已废弃的动词，与 reluctant 同源

entries.definition: not wanting to do something
entries.definitionCN: 不愿意的，最直白的同义表达

entries.definition: slow to act or speak because of doubt
entries.definitionCN: 犹豫的，强调拿不定主意

entries.definition: given or done unwillingly and with bad grace
entries.definitionCN: 勉强的；不情愿的，带有抱怨意味

normalIntro.en: The Latin root luctari means to wrestle, so the word pictures an inner tug of war.
normalIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 luctari 意为「摔跤」，所以这个词画的是一场内心的拔河。

normal.en: Re- plus luctari, to wrestle, gives the picture of wrestling back against a pull.
normal.cn: 前缀 re- 加 luctari「摔跤」，画面是朝着拉力反方向摔回去。

normal.en: The noun reluctance adds -ance, and the adverb reluctantly adds -ly.
normal.cn: 名词 reluctance 加 -ance，副词 reluctantly 加 -ly。

normal.en: The fixed pattern is be reluctant to do something.
normal.cn: 固定句型是 be reluctant to do something。

normal.en: A reluctant hero is someone who never wanted the role in the first place.
normal.cn: a reluctant hero 指从一开始就不想要这个角色的人。

normal.en: Reluctant and reluctance stress the second syllable, re-LUC-tant.
normal.cn: reluctant 与 reluctance 的重音在第二音节，读作 re-LUC-tant。

abstract.en: Imagine a dog bracing its paws while the leash pulls forward.
abstract.cn: 想象一条狗四爪撑地，而牵引绳却往前拉。

abstract.en: See a child holding a door frame on the way to bed.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子被带去睡觉时死死抓住门框。

abstract.en: Think of a smile that arrives half a second too late.
abstract.cn: 想一个慢了半拍才出现的笑容。

examples.en: Many people are reluctant to talk about money.
examples.cn: 许多人不愿意谈论钱。

examples.en: After a long pause she gave a reluctant nod.
examples.cn: 沉默良久，她勉强点了点头。

examples.en: The committee was reluctant to approve the plan.
examples.cn: 委员会不愿批准这项计划。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞拉克坦」——想象坦克不肯往前开，车组用力拉也不动；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 reluctari（反抗、挣扎），由 re-（反）+ luctari（摔跤）构成，现在分词 reluctans 即「正在反抗的」。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as a physical struggle, then narrows into the feeling of not wanting to act and the look that feeling produces.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词起初指身体上的挣扎，后来收窄为「不想行动」的感受，以及这种感受在脸上留下的样子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: feet moving forward while the body pulls back.
core.cn: 核心意象：脚往前迈，身子却往后挣。

branches.en: Resistance felt inside becomes unwillingness and delay.
branches.cn: 内心的抵抗转化为不情愿与拖延。

branches.en: The struggle shows on the face as a strained smile or nod.
branches.cn: 挣扎写在脸上，就成了勉强的笑或点头。

branches.en: The oldest layer keeps the struggle literal, as a horse refusing water.
branches.cn: 最古老的一层保留字面的挣扎，例如马拒绝下水。

branches.en: The inner reluctance and its visible form are the same struggle.
branches.cn: 内心的不情愿与外在的勉强表现是同一种挣扎。

branches.en: Both describe a force meeting a counter-force.
branches.cn: 两者都描述一股力量遇到反向的力量。

intro.en: Reluctant is a Latin participle with a prefix, a root, and a present-participle ending.
intro.cn: reluctant 是拉丁分词，含前缀、词根与现在分词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Re- means back, luctari means to wrestle, and -ant marks the person doing it.
latinIntro.cn: 前缀 re- 表示「反、回」，luctari 表示「摔跤」，词尾 -ant 标记正在做这件事的人。

items.example: Re- turns the wrestling back against the pull.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 让这场摔跤朝拉力反方向进行。

items.example: The luct- root survives in the rare English word luctation.
items.exampleCN: luct- 词根残存在英语罕用词 luctation 中。

items.example: The ending -ant marks the person who is struggling.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ant 标记正在挣扎的那个人。

items.example: Luctari is the verb at the centre of the word.
items.exampleCN: luctari 是这个词的核心动词。

items.example: Reluctari adds re- to luctari.
items.exampleCN: reluctari 在 luctari 前加了 re-。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词词尾
items.example: Reluctance turns the adjective into a noun of state.
items.exampleCN: reluctance 把形容词变成表示状态的名词。

items.example: Reluctantly adds -ly to the adjective.
items.exampleCN: reluctantly 在形容词后加了 -ly。

items.example: Luctation is a rare word that keeps the Latin root visible.
items.exampleCN: luctation 是保留拉丁词根原貌的罕用词。

definition_zh: 依赖；依靠；信任
definition_en: to depend on someone or something for support, help, or truth
core_image: 把自己整个人倚靠在一根结实的柱子上
scene: 停电的夜里，整条街只有这家小店的灯还亮着，邻居们都来买蜡烛。When the power failed, the whole street relied on the little shop that still had candles.
sceneCN: 这里 rely 是「依靠」（第 1 个义项：需要某人或某物提供支持）；句意：停电之后，整条街都依靠那家还有蜡烛的小店。

pos.zh: 依赖；依靠；信任

collocations.phrase: rely on sb to do sth

derivatives.zh: rely 加 -able 构成，义为「可靠的」
rely 加 -ance 构成，义为「依赖；依靠」
reliable 加 -ly 构成，义为「可靠地」

senses.title: To depend on for support
senses.definition: to need someone or something in order to live, work, or succeed
senses.definitionCN: 为生活、工作或成功而需要某人或某物
senses.example: The village relies on the river for drinking water.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村庄依靠这条河获取饮用水。
senses.why: The Latin source means to bind fast, so the core image is leaning your whole weight on something tied in place.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词源意为「牢牢系住」，所以核心画面是把整个人的重量倚在系牢的东西上。

senses.title: To trust someone to be dependable
senses.definition: to believe that someone will do what they promised or that something is true
senses.definitionCN: 相信某人会履行承诺，或相信某事是真的
senses.example: You can rely on her to keep a secret.
senses.exampleCN: 你可以相信她会保守秘密。
senses.why: Leaning on a tied post requires believing it will not move, and that confidence becomes the sense of trust.
senses.whyCN: 倚靠一根系牢的柱子，前提是相信它不会移动，这份信心就发展为「信任」。

intro.en: Rely comes from Old French relier, to bind together, which descends from Latin religare.
intro.cn: rely 来自古法语 relier「绑在一起」，可追溯到拉丁语 religare。

items.en: Religare joins re- with ligare, to bind, and means to tie something fast.
items.cn: religare 由 re- 与 ligare「捆绑」组合，意为牢牢系住。

items.en: The same verb is one of the proposed sources of the noun religion.
items.cn: 这个动词也是名词 religion 的候选词源之一。

items.en: Relier means to bind together, to attach, and to fasten.
items.cn: 古法语 relier 表示绑在一起、连接、系紧。

items.en: English rely first means to attach oneself to a person or a party.
items.cn: 英语中的 rely 最初表示把自己依附于某个人或某个团体。

items.en: From attachment comes dependence, and from dependence comes the everyday sense of trusting.
items.cn: 从依附生出依靠，再从依靠生出日常所说的信任。

note.en: Rely is a binding word at heart, and its family includes reliable and reliance.
note.cn: rely 本质上是一个「系住」的词，词族包括 reliable 与 reliance。

entries.definition: able to be trusted to do what is expected
entries.definitionCN: 可靠的；可信赖的，由 rely 加 -able 构成

entries.definition: the state of depending on someone or something
entries.definitionCN: 依赖；依靠，由 rely 加 -ance 构成

entries.definition: a system of faith and worship
entries.definitionCN: 宗教，与 rely 共享拉丁语 religare 词源

entries.definition: to need someone or something in order to survive or succeed
entries.definitionCN: 依靠；取决于，是最常见的近义词

entries.definition: to believe that someone is honest and will not harm you
entries.definitionCN: 信任，侧重对人的信心

entries.definition: to depend on someone to do what you expect
entries.definitionCN: 指望；依靠，口语中很常用

normalIntro.en: Rely descends from a verb meaning to bind, so the hooks lean on ropes, knots, and steady posts.
normalIntro.cn: rely 源自表示「捆绑」的动词，所以记忆钩子围绕绳索、结和稳固的柱子。

normal.en: The same Latin verb religare also stands behind religion, both about being tied.
normal.cn: 同一个拉丁动词 religare 也是 religion 的来源，两者都关乎「被系住」。

normal.en: Add -able for reliable and -ance for reliance, keeping the y as i before the endings.
normal.cn: 加 -able 得 reliable，加 -ance 得 reliance，加词尾前把 y 变成 i。

normal.en: The past tense relied and the adjective reliable share the same changed spelling.
normal.cn: 过去式 relied 与形容词 reliable 共享同样的拼写变化。

normal.en: The verb always takes on or upon, never a direct object.
normal.cn: 这个动词总是接 on 或 upon，不能直接带宾语。

normal.en: Rely heavily on is the natural phrase for talking about technology and oil.
normal.cn: 谈技术和石油时，rely heavily on 是最自然的说法。

abstract.en: Picture a climber clipping the rope to a steel ring before leaning back.
abstract.cn: 想象攀岩者在后仰之前把绳子扣进钢环。

abstract.en: See a house leaning against an old stone wall in a storm.
abstract.cn: 想象暴风雨中一座房子倚着古老的石墙。

abstract.en: Think of a child holding one finger of an adult in a crowd.
abstract.cn: 想象拥挤人群里，孩子只抓住大人的一根手指。

examples.en: Many small farms rely on rain rather than irrigation.
examples.cn: 许多小农场靠降雨而不是灌溉。

examples.en: We can rely on him to finish the job on time.
examples.cn: 我们可以指望他按时完成工作。

examples.en: The company relies heavily on overseas sales.
examples.cn: 这家公司严重依赖海外销售。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞来」——瑞气来了，可以放心靠上去；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古法语 relier（绑在一起），源自拉丁语 religare（re-「牢牢地」+ ligare「捆绑」）。

sensesIntro.en: One image of leaning on something tied down gives two senses: needing it for support and trusting it to hold.
sensesIntro.cn: 「倚靠系牢之物」这一个画面生出两个义项：需要它提供支撑，以及相信它撑得住。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: leaning your whole weight on a firmly tied post.
core.cn: 核心意象：把整个人的重量倚在系牢的柱子上。

branches.en: The tied post becomes the thing you cannot do without.
branches.cn: 系牢的柱子变成了离不开的依靠。

branches.en: The same post is trusted not to shift, which is the sense of trust.
branches.cn: 同一根柱子被相信不会移动，这就是信任义。

branches.en: Need and trust are two sides of the same leaning.
branches.cn: 需要与信任是同一个倚靠动作的两面。

branches.en: Trust in a person grows from trusting the post to hold.
branches.cn: 对人的信任，是从相信柱子撑得住那里长出来的。

branches.en: Dependence is the plain fact of needing support.
branches.cn: 依赖就是需要支撑这个朴素事实。

intro.en: Rely is a short French borrowing whose Latin parts are still visible in related words.
intro.cn: rely 是一个简短的法语借词，其拉丁成分在相关词中仍清晰可见。

latinIntro.en: Latin re- means back or firmly, and ligare means to bind, so the pair means to bind fast.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁前缀 re- 表示「回、牢牢地」，ligare 表示「捆绑」，两者合起来就是牢牢系住。

items.example: Re- strengthens the binding in religare.
items.exampleCN: 在 religare 中，前缀 re- 强化了捆绑的动作。

items.example: The lig- root returns in ligament and obligation.
items.exampleCN: lig- 词根也出现在 ligament 与 obligation 中。

items.example: Ligare is the source of the lig- root.
items.exampleCN: ligare 是 lig- 词根的来源。

items.example: Reliable means able to be relied on.
items.exampleCN: reliable 意为「可以被依靠的」。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或行为的名词词尾
items.example: Reliance names the state of depending on something.
items.exampleCN: reliance 指依赖的状态。

items.example: Relier is the form English rely comes from.
items.exampleCN: relier 是英语 rely 所来自的形式。

items.example: Religare links rely to religion in form.
items.exampleCN: religare 在形式上把 rely 与 religion 联系起来。

items.example: Ligament shows the lig- root in the body.
items.exampleCN: ligament 展示了 lig- 词根在身体上的应用。

definition_zh: 停留；留下；仍然是；剩下
definition_en: to stay in the same place or condition, or to be left after other things have gone
core_image: 人都走光了，桌上还剩着一只没被收走的杯子
scene: 散场之后，几个学生没有立刻离开，他们留在座位上继续讨论那道题。After the lecture, a few students remained in their seats to argue about the problem.
sceneCN: 这里 remain 是「停留、留下」（第 1 个义项：没有离开原处）；句意：讲座结束后，几个学生留在座位上继续争论那道题。

pos.zh: 停留；留下；仍然是；剩下

derivatives.zh: remain 加 -s 构成的名词，义为「残余；遗迹；遗体」
remain 加 -der 构成，义为「剩余部分」
remain 加 -ing 构成，义为「剩余的」

senses.title: To stay in a place
senses.definition: to stay in the same place instead of leaving with the others
senses.definitionCN: 留在原处，而不随其他人离开
senses.example: Only two guests remained after midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 午夜过后，只有两位客人还留在那里。
senses.why: The Latin verb manere means to stay, and re- adds the idea of staying behind, which gives the plain physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词 manere 意为「停留」，前缀 re- 带来「留在后面」的意味，于是形成最直白的空间义。

senses.title: To continue to be in a state
senses.definition: to continue to be in a particular condition without changing
senses.definitionCN: 继续保持某种状态而不改变
senses.example: The streets remained empty all night.
senses.exampleCN: 整夜街道都空无一人。
senses.why: Staying in a place widens into staying in a condition, such as silence or safety.
senses.whyCN: 「留在某处」扩展为「留在某种状态里」，例如沉默或安全。

senses.title: To be left over
senses.definition: to still exist after other parts have been used, taken, or destroyed
senses.definitionCN: 在其他部分被使用、拿走或毁掉之后仍然存在
senses.example: Little remained of the old town after the fire.
senses.exampleCN: 大火之后，老城几乎没有剩下什么。
senses.why: What stays behind when everyone and everything else has gone is precisely what remains.
senses.whyCN: 当其他人和物都离开或消失后仍留在原地的，正是「剩下的」。

intro.en: Remain comes from Old French remaindre, from Latin remanere, built on re- and manere, to stay.
intro.cn: remain 来自古法语 remaindre，源自拉丁语 remanere，由 re- 与 manere「停留」构成。

items.en: Remanere means to stay behind or to be left, from re- and manere.
items.cn: remanere 意为留在后面或剩下，由 re- 与 manere 构成。

items.en: Manere is also the source of mansion and permanent, both about staying.
items.cn: manere 也是 mansion 与 permanent 的来源，两者都与「停留」有关。

items.en: Remaindre means to stay, to last, and to be left over.
items.cn: 古法语 remaindre 表示停留、持续以及剩下。

items.en: English remain covers staying in a place and continuing in a state.
items.cn: 英语 remain 同时覆盖留在某地与保持某种状态。

items.en: The plural noun remains develops separately for leftovers, ruins, and the bodies of the dead.
items.cn: 复数名词 remains 另行发展出剩饭、遗迹与遗体等含义。

note.en: Remain is the verb of staying, and its family includes the noun remains and the adjective remaining.
note.cn: remain 是表示「停留」的动词，词族包括名词 remains 与形容词 remaining。

entries.definition: what is left after other parts have gone
entries.definitionCN: 残余；遗迹；遗体，由 remain 加 -s 构成

entries.definition: still present when the rest has gone
entries.definitionCN: 剩余的，由 remain 加 -ing 构成

entries.definition: the part that is left over
entries.definitionCN: 剩余部分，与 remain 同源

entries.definition: to continue to be in a place
entries.definitionCN: 停留，是最日常的近义词

entries.definition: to stay somewhere longer than necessary
entries.definitionCN: 逗留；徘徊，带有不愿离开的意味

entries.definition: to continue to exist or happen
entries.definitionCN: 持续存在，侧重不消失

normalIntro.en: The Latin verb manere, to stay, is the spine of this word and of mansion and permanent.
normalIntro.cn: 拉丁动词 manere「停留」是这个词的骨架，也支撑着 mansion 与 permanent。

normal.en: Re- plus manere gives staying behind while everyone else moves on.
normal.cn: 前缀 re- 加 manere，就是别人都走了，它还留在后面。

normal.en: Mansion and permanent share the same root, one a place that stays, one a state that lasts.
normal.cn: mansion 与 permanent 共享同一词根，一个是留下来的房子，一个是持续的状态。

normal.en: Add -s and the word becomes a noun for leftovers and ruins.
normal.cn: 加 -s 就变成名词，指剩饭与遗迹。

normal.en: The pattern remain silent teaches the linking use: remain plus adjective.
normal.cn: remain silent 这个搭配说明了它的连系用法：remain 加形容词。

normal.en: It remains to be seen is a fixed sentence opener in news writing.
normal.cn: it remains to be seen 是新闻写作中固定的句子开头。

abstract.en: Picture a single cup on a table after the whole party has left.
abstract.cn: 想象聚会散尽后，桌上只留下一个杯子。

abstract.en: See a lighthouse still standing after the village has been abandoned.
abstract.cn: 想象村庄废弃之后，灯塔仍然立着。

abstract.en: Think of a light left on in a window all night.
abstract.cn: 想一扇窗里彻夜亮着的灯。

examples.en: Please remain seated until the plane has stopped.
examples.cn: 飞机停稳之前请留在座位上。

examples.en: The reason for the delay remains a mystery.
examples.cn: 延误的原因仍然是个谜。

examples.en: Very little remained of the original building.
examples.cn: 原来的建筑几乎没有剩下什么。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞梅」——梅花谢了，枝上还剩一朵；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古法语 remaindre，源自拉丁语 remanere（re-「留在后面」+ manere「停留」）。

sensesIntro.en: Staying in a place becomes staying in a state and then being what is left when everything else is gone.
sensesIntro.cn: 留在某处，进而变成留在某种状态，再变成其他一切消失后尚存的部分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one cup left on the table after everyone has gone.
core.cn: 核心意象：人都走光后，桌上还剩一只杯子。

branches.en: The cup stays where it was, which is the plain sense of remaining in place.
branches.cn: 杯子留在原处，这就是最直白的「停留」义。

branches.en: Staying in a place stretches into staying in a condition.
branches.cn: 留在某处被拉长成留在某种状态里。

branches.en: When everything else is taken away, what stays is what is left over.
branches.cn: 其他一切被拿走之后，留下来的就是剩余之物。

branches.en: Both senses keep the same stillness at the centre.
branches.cn: 两个义项的中心都是同一种静止不动。

branches.en: Physical staying and ongoing state share one root, manere.
branches.cn: 空间上的停留与状态的延续共享同一个词根 manere。

intro.en: Remain is a French-shaped verb whose Latin prefix and root still show in related words.
intro.cn: remain 是法语形态的动词，其拉丁前缀与词根在相关词中仍然可见。

latinIntro.en: Latin re- means back or behind, and manere means to stay, so the verb means to stay behind.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁前缀 re- 表示「回、在后」，manere 表示「停留」，合起来即「留在后面」。

items.example: Re- gives the sense of staying behind.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 带来「留在后面」的含义。

items.example: The man- root returns in mansion and permanent.
items.exampleCN: man- 词根也出现在 mansion 与 permanent 中。

items.example: Manere is the verb at the heart of remain.
items.exampleCN: manere 是 remain 的核心动词。

items.meaning: more than one, or a mass noun
items.example: Remains turns the verb into a plural noun.
items.exampleCN: remains 把动词变成复数名词。

items.example: Remaining describes what is still there.
items.exampleCN: remaining 描述依然存在的部分。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作结果的名词词尾
items.example: Remainder names the part left over.
items.exampleCN: remainder 指剩下的部分。

items.example: Mansion keeps the sense of a place where one stays.

definition_zh: 残余；遗迹；遗体；剩余物
definition_en: the parts that are left after the rest has been used, destroyed, or taken away
core_image: 沙土里露出半截石墙，房屋本身早已不见
scene: 考古队在麦田下面挖出了几段石墙和一批陶片。Under the wheat field, the team found the remains of a small Roman house.
sceneCN: 这里 remains 是「遗迹」（第 1 个义项：古代建筑残留的部分）；句意：在麦田下面，考古队发现了一座小罗马房屋的遗迹。

senses.title: What is left after destruction
senses.definition: the parts of a building, object, or settlement that survive after the rest has gone
senses.definitionCN: 建筑、器物或聚落在其余部分消失后仍然存在的部分
senses.example: The remains of the city wall can still be seen.
senses.exampleCN: 城墙的残迹仍依稀可见。
senses.why: Remains is simply the plural of the verb used as a noun, so it names whatever has stayed behind while the rest went.
senses.whyCN: remains 就是动词的复数形式被用作名词，指其余部分消失后仍然留下来的东西。

senses.title: The body of a dead person
senses.definition: the body of a dead person or animal, used with care and formality
senses.definitionCN: 死者或死动物的身体，用于谨慎、正式的场合
senses.example: The remains were returned to the family.
senses.exampleCN: 遗骸被交还给了家属。
senses.why: What is left of a person after death is treated with the same respectful word used for ruins.
senses.whyCN: 人死之后所留下的部分，也用这个对待遗迹般的敬重字眼。

senses.title: Leftover food or material
senses.definition: the food or material that was not finished or used
senses.definitionCN: 没有吃完或用完的食物或材料
senses.example: She packed the remains of the cake into a box.
senses.exampleCN: 她把剩下的蛋糕装进了盒子。
senses.why: The everyday sense is the most literal: whatever is left on the table or in the workshop.
senses.whyCN: 最日常的义项最字面：桌上或作坊里没被用掉的那一部分。

intro.en: Remains is the plural of remain used as a noun; the noun developed in English rather than in Latin.
intro.cn: remains 是动词 remain 的复数形式被用作名词，这一名词用法在英语中发展而成，而非直接来自拉丁语。

items.en: Remanere, to stay behind, supplies the verb that the noun is built on.
items.cn: remanere「留在后面」提供了这个名词所依附的动词。

items.en: Old French remaindre gives English the verb remain.
items.cn: 古法语 remaindre 给英语带来了动词 remain。

items.en: The plural remains is used for what is left of a building or a meal.
items.cn: 十五世纪起，复数 remains 用来指建筑或饭菜剩下的部分。

items.en: The word becomes a formal and respectful term for the bodies of the dead.
items.cn: 十七世纪起，这个词成为指称死者遗体的正式而敬重的说法。

items.en: Archaeology fixes the sense of ancient remains, and the word stays plural in all uses.
items.cn: 考古学固定了「古代遗迹」这一义项，而这个词在各类用法中都保持复数。

note.en: Remains is a plural-only noun, and it stands beside words for ruins, relics, and leftovers.
note.cn: remains 是只用复数的名词，与表示废墟、遗物与残羹的词相邻。

entries.definition: to stay behind or continue to exist
entries.definitionCN: 停留；剩下，是 remains 的动词来源

entries.definition: still there after the rest has gone
entries.definitionCN: 剩余的，是同一词根的形容词形式

entries.definition: a small part left after the rest is gone
entries.definitionCN: 残余；零头，与 remains 意义接近但拼写不同

entries.definition: the broken parts of an old building
entries.definitionCN: 废墟；遗址，侧重破败状态

entries.definition: an object surviving from an earlier time
entries.definitionCN: 遗物；文物，强调有保存价值

entries.definition: food not eaten at a meal
entries.definitionCN: 剩饭；剩余食物，口语常用

normalIntro.en: Remains is the plural of remain, so the hooks all come back to things that stayed behind.
normalIntro.cn: remains 就是 remain 的复数，所以记忆钩子都回到「留下来的东西」。

normal.en: Treat it as a plural noun: the remains of a temple, the remains of a meal.
normal.cn: 把它当复数名词用：寺庙的遗迹、一餐的剩余。

normal.en: Human remains is the respectful phrase in news reports and official writing.
normal.cn: human remains 是新闻报道与官方文书中的敬重说法。

normal.en: Remains never takes a singular form in these senses, so avoid writing a remain.
normal.cn: 这些义项下 remains 没有单数形式，不要写成 a remain。

normal.en: The verb remain is the base, and the noun adds only an s.
normal.cn: 动词 remain 是基础，名词只加了一个 s。

normal.en: Archaeology reports often begin with the remains of a settlement.
normal.cn: 考古报告常常以某处聚落的遗迹开头。

abstract.en: Picture a broken wall sticking out of a field, the house long gone.
abstract.cn: 想象一段断墙从田里露出来，房子早已不在。

abstract.en: See a few crumbs and an empty plate after a birthday cake.
abstract.cn: 想象生日蛋糕之后留下的一点碎屑和空盘子。

abstract.en: Think of bones carefully laid in a wooden box.
abstract.cn: 想木盒里被小心安放的骸骨。

examples.en: The remains of the meal were given to the dog.
examples.cn: 剩下的饭菜给了狗。

examples.en: Workers uncovered human remains at the building site.
examples.cn: 工人在工地发现了人类遗骸。

examples.en: The museum displays remains from the Bronze Age.
examples.cn: 博物馆展出青铜时代的遗物。

root: 动词 remain 的复数名词化，源自拉丁语 remanere（re-「留在后面」+ manere「停留」）。

sensesIntro.en: One plural noun covers ruins, corpses, and leftovers, because all three are what stayed after the rest went.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个复数名词涵盖遗迹、遗体与剩饭，因为三者都是其余部分消失后留下来的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a half-buried wall where a house once stood.
core.cn: 核心意象：房屋早已消失，只剩半埋在土里的石墙。

branches.en: Stone that outlasts its building is the archaeological sense.
branches.cn: 比建筑更长寿的石头，就是考古意义上的遗迹。

branches.en: What outlasts a person is named with the same respectful word.
branches.cn: 比人更长久留存的部分，也用同一个敬重的词来命名。

branches.en: What outlasts a meal is the plainest everyday leftover.
branches.cn: 比一餐饭更长久留存的，就是最日常的剩饭。

branches.en: Both ruins and human remains call for careful, formal language.
branches.cn: 遗迹与遗体都需要谨慎、正式的表达。

branches.en: Both are simply what the rest of the world left behind.
branches.cn: 两者都只是其余世界留下的那部分。

intro.en: Remains has no prefix of its own beyond the verb it comes from, but its Latin root is still clear.
intro.cn: remains 除所依附的动词外没有独立前缀，但其拉丁词根仍然清楚。

latinIntro.en: The chain runs from Latin manere, to stay, through remanere, to stay behind, to the English verb remain.
latinIntro.cn: 这条链从拉丁语 manere「停留」经 remanere「留在后面」到英语动词 remain。

items.example: The man- root also appears in mansion.
items.exampleCN: man- 词根也出现在 mansion 中。

items.example: Manere is the oldest layer of the family.
items.exampleCN: manere 是这个词族最古老的一层。

items.example: Re- adds the idea of staying behind.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 增添了「留在后面」的意思。

items.example: Remanere is the direct Latin ancestor.
items.exampleCN: remanere 是直接的拉丁祖先。

items.example: The -s makes the verb into a plural noun.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -s 把动词变成复数名词。

items.example: Remnant is a close cousin in meaning.
items.exampleCN: remnant 在语义上是近亲。

items.example: Permanent keeps the same staying root.
items.exampleCN: permanent 保留同一个「停留」词根。

items.example: Mansion shows the root in a place of dwelling.
items.exampleCN: mansion 展示了这个词根在居住场所上的用法。

definition_zh: 评论说；谈论；注意到；评论
definition_en: to say something that shows what you have noticed, or the words you say
core_image: 眼睛在人群里忽然停住，指着某处说了一句话
scene: 她翻到照片最后一页，忽然说这地方她小时候来过。She turned to the last page and remarked that she had been there as a child.
sceneCN: 这里 remark 是「评论说」（第 1 个义项：说出自己注意到的事）；句意：她翻到最后一页，评论说自己小时候去过那里。

pos.zh: 评论说；谈到
谈论；评论
评论；言辞

remarkable 加 -ly 构成，义为「非凡地；出乎意料地」

senses.title: To say something about what you notice
senses.definition: to say something, often briefly, as a comment on what you have seen or heard
senses.definitionCN: 就所见所闻简短地说出看法
senses.example: He remarked that the room was unusually quiet.
senses.exampleCN: 他说这房间安静得反常。
senses.why: The French source means to mark, so the core picture is noticing a detail and then pointing it out in words.
senses.whyCN: 法语词源意为「做标记」，所以核心画面是先注意到某个细节，再用话语把它指出来。

senses.title: To notice something
senses.definition: to see or notice something and mentally mark it as important
senses.definitionCN: 看到或注意到某事，并在心里把它标记为重要
senses.example: She remarked a strange smell as she entered.
senses.exampleCN: 她进门时注意到一股奇怪的气味。
senses.why: Before a remark can be spoken it must be marked in the mind, which is the older layer of the verb.
senses.whyCN: 话未出口先在心里做标记，这正是这个动词更古老的一层含义。

senses.title: A spoken or written comment
senses.definition: a short statement that gives an opinion or draws attention to something
senses.definitionCN: 表达看法或引起注意的简短话语
senses.example: His opening remarks were short and warm.
senses.exampleCN: 他的开场白简短而温暖。
senses.why: The noun keeps the same mark: a remark is a small marker placed on a topic by the speaker.
senses.whyCN: 名词保留同一个「标记」：评论就是说话者在话题上留下的小标记。

intro.en: Remark comes from French remarquer, to mark or note, built on re- and marquer.
intro.cn: remark 来自法语 remarquer「标记、注意」，由 re- 与 marquer 构成。

items.en: The mark family probably goes back to a Germanic root for a boundary or sign.
items.cn: 表示「标记」的这组词一般认为可追溯到日耳曼语中表示边界或记号的词根。

items.en: Marquer means to mark, and remarquer means to mark out or notice.
items.cn: 古法语 marquer 表示做记号，remarquer 表示标出或注意到。

items.en: Remarquer develops the sense of saying something that one has noticed.
items.cn: remarquer 发展出「就注意到的事说一句」的含义。

items.en: English remark first means to notice, then to utter a comment.
items.cn: 英语 remark 先表示「注意到」，随后表示「说出评论」。

items.en: The noun remark settles into the sense of a short comment or a formal opening address.
items.cn: 名词 remark 固定为简短评论或正式开场白的含义。

note.en: Remark belongs to the mark family and gives us remarkable, while comment is its closest everyday partner.
note.cn: remark 属于 mark 词族，并派生出 remarkable；comment 是它最接近的日常近义词。

entries.definition: unusual and worth noticing
entries.definitionCN: 非凡的；值得注意的，由 remark 加 -able 构成

entries.definition: in a surprising or unusual way
entries.definitionCN: 非凡地；出乎意料地

entries.definition: a visible sign or spot
entries.definitionCN: 记号；痕迹，是 remark 的词根来源

entries.definition: a spoken or written opinion about something
entries.definitionCN: 评论；意见，与 remark 名词义几乎同义

entries.definition: to notice something and sometimes mention it
entries.definitionCN: 观察；评论说，兼具看与说

entries.definition: to speak about something briefly
entries.definitionCN: 提到；说起，不强调评论色彩

normalIntro.en: Remark is literally to mark again in the mind before marking it in words.
normalIntro.cn: remark 字面上是先在心中再做一个标记，然后用话语标出来。

normal.en: Re- plus mark gives marking something so that it stands out.
normal.cn: 前缀 re- 加 mark，就是给它做个记号让它显出来。

normal.en: Remarkable is what deserves a remark, and remarkably tells how it was done.
normal.cn: remarkable 是值得被评论的，remarkably 说明是以何种方式做到的。

normal.en: Remarks in the plural often means a formal speech at an opening.
normal.cn: 复数 remarks 常指开幕时的正式致辞。

normal.en: The verb is usually followed by that or on.
normal.cn: 这个动词后面通常接 that 从句或 on。

normal.en: A casual remark can still carry a lot of weight.
normal.cn: a casual remark 随口一说，也可能很有分量。

abstract.en: Imagine a finger pointing at a small detail and a voice naming it.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指指向某个细节，同时有个声音把它说出来。

abstract.en: See a pencil making a small tick beside a line of text.
abstract.cn: 想象铅笔在文字旁划出一个小小的勾。

abstract.en: Think of a guest standing up to say a few words at a table.
abstract.cn: 想一位客人在餐桌旁站起来说几句话。

examples.en: She remarked on how much the town had changed.
examples.cn: 她谈到这座小镇变化有多大。

examples.en: He made a rude remark and left the room.
examples.cn: 他留下一句粗鲁的话就离开了房间。

examples.en: The chair opened the meeting with a few remarks.
examples.cn: 主席以几句开场白开始了会议。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞马克」——在瑞丽买一枚马克笔，边看边做记号；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 法语 remarquer（标记、注意），由 re-（再次）与 marquer（做记号）构成。

sensesIntro.en: Marking a detail in the mind and marking it in words produce the senses of noticing, saying, and the comment itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 在心里标记一个细节、再用话语标记它，就生出「注意到」「说道」以及「评论」三个义项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: eyes stopping on a detail, then a voice naming it.
core.cn: 核心意象：目光在某个细节上停住，随后有个声音把它说出来。

branches.en: A marked detail is spoken aloud, which is the everyday verb.
branches.cn: 被标记的细节被说出来，就是最日常的动词用法。

branches.en: Before speech there is silent marking, the older sense of noticing.
branches.cn: 说话之前先有无声的标记，即更古老的「注意到」。

branches.en: The words left behind are themselves the mark, hence the noun.
branches.cn: 留下的那些话本身就是记号，于是有了名词用法。

branches.en: Saying and the thing said are two sides of one mark.
branches.cn: 说出来的动作与被说出的内容，是同一个标记的两面。

branches.en: Noticing is the gate through which every remark passes.
branches.cn: 「注意到」是每一句评论都必须经过的门。

intro.en: Remark is a French verb that entered English with both its prefix and its root intact.
intro.cn: remark 是带着前缀与词根一起进入英语的法语动词。

latinIntro.en: The prefix re- adds the idea of again, and the mark root carries the sense of a sign or boundary.
latinIntro.cn: 前缀 re- 增添「再次」的意思，mark 词根带有「记号、边界」的含义。

items.example: Re- marks the action as repeated or emphatic.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 让动作带上重复或强调的意味。

items.example: The mark root also gives the English word mark.
items.exampleCN: mark 词根也产生了英语单词 mark。

items.example: Marquer is the French verb behind remark.
items.exampleCN: marquer 是 remark 背后的法语动词。

items.example: Remarquer is borrowed almost whole into English.
items.exampleCN: remarquer 几乎被整体借入英语。

items.example: Remarkable means worth remarking on.
items.exampleCN: remarkable 意为「值得被谈论的」。

items.example: Remarkably adds -ly to the adjective.
items.exampleCN: remarkably 在形容词后加了 -ly。

items.example: Marker shows the plain mark root with an agent ending.
items.exampleCN: marker 展示了 mark 词根加施事词尾的形态。

items.meaning: an easily seen feature of a landscape
items.example: Landmark joins land with the same marking root.
items.exampleCN: landmark 把 land 与同一个标记词根组合起来。

definition_zh: 非凡的；值得注意的；惊人的；值得称道的
definition_en: unusual in a way that is worth noticing, often in a good sense
core_image: 一群普通房子中间忽然立起一座通体发亮的塔
scene: 那支球队从垫底一路打进决赛，整个城市都在谈论这件事。The team climbed from last place to the final, a remarkable run that the whole city talked about.
sceneCN: 这里 remarkable 是「非凡的」（第 1 个义项：不同寻常且值得注意）；句意：这支球队从最后一名一路打进决赛，这段非凡的历程被全城谈论。

pos.zh: 非凡的；值得注意的；惊人的；值得称道的

derivatives.zh: remarkable 加 -ly 构成，义为「非凡地；出乎意料地」
remarkable 的动词来源，义为「评论；注意到」

senses.title: Unusual and worth noticing
senses.definition: unusual enough to attract attention and deserve comment
senses.definitionCN: 不同寻常到足以引起注意并值得一说
senses.example: The bridge is a remarkable piece of engineering.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥是一项非凡的工程。
senses.why: Remarkable is literally what can be remarked on, so anything that draws comment is remarkable.
senses.whyCN: remarkable 字面上是「可以被谈论的」，因此任何引人评论的事物都称得上非凡。

senses.title: Surprising in degree
senses.definition: surprising because it is much greater or smaller than expected
senses.definitionCN: 因为比预期大得多或小得多而令人惊讶
senses.example: There is a remarkable similarity between the two paintings.
senses.exampleCN: 这两幅画之间有惊人的相似。
senses.why: When the amount of something passes expectation, it forces a remark, which is the surprise sense.
senses.whyCN: 当某事物的程度超出预期，人就会忍不住开口评论，这就是「惊人」这一义项。

senses.title: Deserving praise
senses.definition: so good that people admire it and talk about it with approval
senses.definitionCN: 好到让人钦佩并带着赞许谈论
senses.example: She made a remarkable recovery after the operation.
senses.exampleCN: 手术之后她的恢复情况非常了不起。
senses.why: The same notice turns into praise when the thing noticed is good rather than merely strange.
senses.whyCN: 当被注意到的东西不只是奇特而且是好的，同一份注意就转为赞许。

intro.en: Remarkable is an English adjective built from the verb remark with the ending -able.
intro.cn: remarkable 是英语中由动词 remark 加词尾 -able 构成的形容词。

items.en: The verb remarquer, to mark or notice, supplies the base of the word.
items.cn: 古法语动词 remarquer「标记、注意」提供了这个词的基础。

items.en: Remark enters English, and -able is soon added to form an adjective.
items.cn: remark 进入英语后不久就加上 -able 构成形容词。

items.en: Remarkable first means worthy of being noted or commented on.
items.cn: remarkable 最初意为「值得被记下或谈论的」。

items.en: The word widens to mean excellent or extraordinary, especially in praise.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，词义扩展到「卓越的、非凡的」，多用于称赞。

items.en: Modern usage often prefers it for surprising facts and impressive achievements.
items.cn: 现代用法常用它形容令人惊讶的事实与令人印象深刻的成就。

note.en: Remarkable is the adjective of remark, and it stands beside words for extraordinary and impressive.
note.cn: remarkable 是 remark 的形容词，与表示非凡与令人印象深刻的词相邻。

entries.definition: very noticeable because of being unusual
entries.definitionCN: 引人注目的，强调视觉或印象上的冲击

normalIntro.en: Remarkable means worth remarking on, so the whole word rests on the verb remark.
normalIntro.cn: remarkable 意为「值得被谈论的」，整个词都依托于动词 remark。

normal.en: Add -able to remark and you get the quality of deserving comment.
normal.cn: 在 remark 后加 -able，就得到「值得被评论」这种性质。

normal.en: Change the ending to -ably for the adverb remarkably.
normal.cn: 把词尾换成 -ably 就得到副词 remarkably。

normal.en: Put un- in front and the word means nothing worth noticing.
normal.cn: 在前面加 un-，这个词就表示「没有值得注意之处」。

normal.en: Remarkable progress and a remarkable achievement are the two most common pairings.
normal.cn: remarkable progress 与 a remarkable achievement 是最常见的两个搭配。

normal.en: The word often points to praise, not just surprise.
normal.cn: 这个词常带有赞许，而不只是惊讶。

abstract.en: Picture one lit tower among rows of ordinary houses.
abstract.cn: 想象一排普通房屋中忽然立起一座发亮的塔。

abstract.en: See a crowd turning its head at the same moment.
abstract.cn: 想象人群在同一瞬间转过头去。

abstract.en: Think of a record time that makes the announcer pause.
abstract.cn: 想一个让解说员停顿的记录成绩。

examples.en: The patient made a remarkable recovery.
examples.cn: 这位病人恢复得非常好。

examples.en: It is remarkable how quickly the children learned.
examples.cn: 孩子们学得这么快，实在令人惊讶。

examples.en: The two brothers share a remarkable resemblance.
examples.cn: 这两兄弟长得惊人地相像。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞马克伯」——想象一位叫马克伯的人在瑞丽做出惊人之举；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 由动词 remark（评论；注意到）加形容词词尾 -able 构成，词根可追至法语 marquer「做记号」。

sensesIntro.en: Anything worth remarking on can be remarkable, whether it is merely strange, surprisingly large, or genuinely excellent.
sensesIntro.cn: 任何值得一说的东西都可以叫 remarkable，无论它只是奇特、出人意料地大，还是确实优秀。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one lit tower standing among ordinary houses.
core.cn: 核心意象：普通房屋之间立着一座发亮的塔。

branches.en: What draws a mark draws attention, which is the core adjective sense.
branches.cn: 能留下标记的东西自然引人注意，这是核心形容词义。

branches.en: A degree far beyond expectation forces a comment of surprise.
branches.cn: 远超预期的程度会逼出一句惊讶的评论。

branches.en: When the noticed thing is good, notice becomes praise.
branches.cn: 当被注意到的事物是好的，注意就变成赞许。

branches.en: Both rest on the same act of mental marking.
branches.cn: 两者都建立在同一个心里做标记的动作上。

branches.en: Surprise and admiration are the two common colours of the word.
branches.cn: 惊讶与钦佩是这个词最常见的两种色彩。

intro.en: Remarkable stacks an English adjective ending onto a French verb borrowed into English.
intro.cn: remarkable 在借入英语的法语动词上叠加了一个英语形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: The -able ending comes from Latin -abilis, meaning able to be, and the base is the marking root.
latinIntro.cn: 词尾 -able 来自拉丁语 -abilis，意为「能够被……的」，其基础是表示标记的词根。

items.example: Re- intensifies the marking in remark.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 加强了 remark 中「标记」的动作。

items.example: The mark root is shared with marker and landmark.
items.exampleCN: mark 词根与 marker、landmark 共用。

items.example: Remarkable means worth remarking on.
items.exampleCN: remarkable 意为「值得被谈论的」。

items.example: Remarkably turns the adjective into an adverb.
items.exampleCN: remarkably 把形容词变成副词。

items.example: Unremarkable means not worth noticing.
items.exampleCN: unremarkable 表示「不值得注意的」。

items.example: Marquer supplies the base of the family.
items.exampleCN: marquer 提供了这一词族的基础。

items.meaning: a tool or sign that marks
items.example: Marker pairs the mark root with an agent ending.
items.exampleCN: marker 把 mark 词根与施事词尾组合在一起。

items.meaning: a feature that marks a place
items.example: Landmark keeps the boundary sense of the old root.
items.exampleCN: landmark 保留了古老词根的「边界」意味。

平淡无奇的

definition_zh: 非凡地；显著地；出乎意料地
definition_en: in a way that is unusual and surprising, or to a surprising degree
core_image: 所有数字都很平常，唯独一栏高得刺眼
scene: 这个孩子只练了半年，就已经能完整弹下那首曲子。For a child who had practised for only six months, she played the piece remarkably well.
sceneCN: 这里 remarkably 是「出乎意料地」（第 2 个义项：达到令人惊讶的程度）；句意：对一个只练了半年的孩子来说，她把这首曲子弹得惊人地好。

pos.zh: 非凡地；显著地；出乎意料地

derivatives.zh: remarkably 的形容词来源，义为「非凡的」
该词族的动词基础，义为「评论；注意到」

senses.title: In an unusual and striking way
senses.definition: in a way that stands out from what is normal and deserves attention
senses.definitionCN: 以超越常态、值得注意的方式
senses.example: The old engine ran remarkably smoothly.
senses.exampleCN: 这台旧发动机运转得异常平稳。
senses.why: The adverb simply carries the adjective meaning into how an action is done, so the action itself becomes worth remarking on.
senses.whyCN: 副词只是把形容词的意思转移到动作的方式上，于是这个动作本身变得值得一说。

senses.title: To a surprising degree
senses.definition: used to say that an amount or level is much greater or smaller than expected
senses.definitionCN: 用于说明数量或程度比预期大得多或小得多
senses.example: Remarkably few people came to the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 来开会的人少得令人惊讶。
senses.why: When the size of something breaks expectation, the comment that follows is a comment on degree, which is this sense.
senses.whyCN: 当事物的量突破预期，随之而来的评论就是针对程度的，这就是第二义项。

intro.en: Remarkably is remarkable plus the adverb ending -ly, and the whole family goes back to the French verb remarquer.
intro.cn: remarkably 由 remarkable 加副词词尾 -ly 构成，整族词可追溯到法语动词 remarquer。

items.en: Remarquer means to mark, to notice, and later to comment.
items.cn: remarquer 表示做记号、注意，后来也表示评论。

items.en: The adjective remarkable is formed from remark with -able.
items.cn: 形容词 remarkable 由 remark 加 -able 构成。

items.en: The adverb remarkably appears soon after, adding -ly to the adjective.
items.cn: 副词 remarkably 随后出现，在形容词后加上 -ly。

items.en: Remarkably begins to work as an intensifier before adjectives such as well and little.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，remarkably 开始用在 well、little 等形容词前起强调作用。

items.en: Today it most often signals a surprising degree in reporting and description.
items.cn: 今天它最常用于报道与描写中，标示一种令人惊讶的程度。

note.en: Remarkably is the adverb of the remark family, and it stands near other degree adverbs.
note.cn: remarkably 是 remark 词族的副词，与其它程度副词相邻。

entries.definition: unusual and worth noticing
entries.definitionCN: 非凡的；值得注意的，是 remarkably 的形容词

entries.definition: in an ordinary way that draws no attention
entries.definitionCN: 平淡无奇地，由否定前缀 un- 构成

entries.definition: to comment or notice
entries.definitionCN: 评论；注意到，是该词族的动词

entries.definition: in a way that is very noticeable
entries.definitionCN: 显著地；惊人地，强调视觉冲击

entries.definition: especially, in a way worth noting
entries.definitionCN: 尤其；显著地，偏正式

entries.definition: in a way that is unexpected
entries.definitionCN: 出乎意料地，侧重与预期相反

normalIntro.en: Remarkably is built in three steps from remark, so the hooks follow the endings.
normalIntro.cn: remarkably 从 remark 分三步构成，记忆钩子顺着词尾走。

normal.en: Remark, then remarkable, then remarkably: verb, adjective, adverb.
normal.cn: remark、remarkable、remarkably，依次是动词、形容词、副词。

normal.en: The ending -ly marks an adverb, so remarkably describes how something is done.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ly 标记副词，所以 remarkably 描述事情是「怎样」做的。

normal.en: It often intensifies well, similar, few, and little.
normal.cn: 它常用来强化 well、similar、few、little 这类词。

normal.en: Remarkably few is a common way to report a surprisingly small number.
normal.cn: remarkably few 是报道「数量少得惊人」的常用说法。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with remark, which is a verb or a countable noun.
normal.cn: 不要与 remark 混淆，后者是动词或可数名词。

abstract.en: Picture a bar chart where one column shoots above all the others.
abstract.cn: 想象一张柱状图，其中一根柱子高过其它所有柱子。

abstract.en: See a small child lifting a case twice her size.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小女孩提起比她大一倍的箱子。

abstract.en: Think of a clock that runs without a single second of error.
abstract.cn: 想一只一秒都不差的钟。

examples.en: The two designs are remarkably similar.
examples.cn: 这两个设计惊人地相似。

examples.en: She recovered remarkably quickly after the surgery.
examples.cn: 手术之后她恢复得异常迅速。

examples.en: Remarkably, no one was hurt in the crash.
examples.cn: 令人惊讶的是，撞车事故里没有人受伤。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞马克伯利」——想象马克伯在瑞丽的表现好得让所有人回头；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 由 remarkable 加副词词尾 -ly 构成，词根可追至法语 remarquer「做记号、注意」。

sensesIntro.en: The adverb either describes how something stands out or measures how far a quantity departs from expectation.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个副词要么描述某事如何突出，要么衡量某个量偏离预期的程度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one column in a chart towering over the rest.
core.cn: 核心意象：图表中一根柱子高出其余所有。

branches.en: Doing something in a marked way is the qualitative sense.
branches.cn: 以带标记的方式做事，是性质层面的义项。

branches.en: Measuring how far a figure departs from expectation is the quantitative sense.
branches.cn: 衡量数字偏离预期多远，是程度层面的义项。

branches.en: Both turn a mental mark into a spoken emphasis.
branches.cn: 两者都把心里的标记转化为口头强调。

branches.en: Degree adverbs often sit right before the word they measure.
branches.cn: 程度副词常紧贴它所修饰的词之前。

branches.en: The manner sense usually follows the verb it describes.
branches.cn: 方式义通常跟在它所描述的动词之后。

intro.en: Remarkably carries the mark root plus an adjective ending and then an adverb ending.
intro.cn: remarkably 携带 mark 词根，并依次加上形容词词尾和副词词尾。

latinIntro.en: The -able ending comes from Latin and the -ly ending is native English, so the word mixes two layers.
latinIntro.cn: -able 词尾来自拉丁语，-ly 词尾是英语本族成分，因此这个词混合了两层来源。

items.example: Re- strengthens the marking in the base word.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 强化了基础词中的标记动作。

items.example: The mark root is visible in marker and landmark.
items.exampleCN: mark 词根在 marker 与 landmark 中清晰可见。

items.example: Remarkable means worth remarking on.
items.exampleCN: remarkable 意为「值得被谈论的」。

items.example: The ending -ly turns the adjective into an adverb.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 把形容词变成副词。

items.example: Unremarkably means in a way that draws no notice.
items.exampleCN: unremarkably 表示「不引人注意地」。

items.example: Marquer lies at the base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: marquer 位于整个词族的底层。

items.meaning: a sign or tool that marks
items.example: Marker joins the mark root with -er.
items.exampleCN: marker 把 mark 词根与 -er 组合。

items.example: Remarkable is the adjective immediately behind the adverb.
items.exampleCN: remarkable 是这个副词直接依托的形容词。
